insight.title: The Center of the Earth Is Younger Than Its Crust
insight.subtitle: Because gravity warps time, the interior of our planet has experienced less history than the surface.
insight.notificationHook: Earth's core is younger than its crust

sections.text: Deep beneath our feet, the molten iron core of the Earth is ticking at a slower rate than the solid ground we walk on.
According to Einstein's relativity, gravity warps the fabric of time. The closer an object is to a massive body's center, the stronger the gravitational pull, and the slower time passes.
Scientists calculated that this invisible lag has accumulated over billions of years. As a result, the very center of our planet is physically two and a half years younger than its crust.
Our planet is traveling through time at two different speeds.
